text: ### Capacity acceptance — 2026-10-08

The parent accepts R009 as the third substantial deduction under the pinned corpus. The contribution is the uniform local moment and flow-splitting sufficiency proof for arbitrary edge channels, including channels approaching or equal to perfect transmission. The final contribution audit recommends acceptance after checking variable-interaction Ising, Potts and robust-reconstruction literature and proposed standard reductions. Capacity formalism and the near-perfect ray example are not claimed as new.

No accepted theorem or substantial-finding count is added. The parity audit and cubic-reservoir work continue independently.
### Parity proof acceptance — 2026-10-08

The independent audit passes i05 Propositions 1–3 and retains the classical attribution of the Q/F/C criterion. The new i06 report proves a proposed full-range scalar Hecke trace estimate and rough-composite cancellation, but does not obtain the initial trace-weighted rough correlation. Its exact RP interface, and weaker MT-lower alternative, include the modulus-dependent tail budget needed to reach simultaneous primitive roots. Those estimates and the reservoir CR remain unproved. The new SL/CC arguments are not separately independently audited or promoted.
### Parity final acceptance — 2026-10-08

Decision: the second substantive-discovery objective is met by R008 on the qualified accepted-corpus basis. It is one finding, already committed separately for mathematical acceptance, with this final-review integration completing its significance assessment. Worldwide priority, independent validation of upstream truth, external peer review and formal certification are not claimed. Gaussian and cubic lanes remain respectively demoted and unclosed; neither is counted toward success. No further task is launched or publication attempted.

Primary-source checks of Arapura Theorems 3.2–3.4 and Ein–Lazarsfeld Theorem 1 agree with the restrictions quoted in the report. The separate independent proof review remains pending.

Decision: continue with the exact rank-two transfer problem in §7 of the report. The new task must use the actual dyadic weights, test controllability/observability and ordinary invariant subspaces, and reject mere similarity constructions. If that approach yields only an elementary or known obstruction, it must attempt a materially different construction. No accepted-finding count is increased.

The fresh round-4 audit completed successfully. [R005](../findings/R005-operator-reflection-obstruction.md) closes the entire specified T_a=S+M_aV family as ordinary-ISP counterexamples: the plus and minus weighted-reflection spaces are closed invariant half-spaces, with zero intersection and dense nonclosed sum. The nonclosedness refinement uses the actual infinite normalizer's essential unboundedness. No substantive correction to the original half-space proof was needed. The historical provider failure has no bearing on this proof verdict.

The completed report constructs a proposed convergent annihilator of the central orbit for Q=S+RV and extends the construction to every S+M_rV with bounded measurable complex coordinate/base multiplier r. Its new mechanism is a uniform bound ||C^n||≤exp(−n^4) obtained from the exact infinite normalizer; this dominates the quadratic growth of coordinate-weight inverses and the triangular recursion coefficients. If correct, this closes the whole bounded-multiplier lane rather than merely the failed reflection ansatz. Separate direct kernel estimates claim empty point spectra for Q and its adjoint.

The parent read the full proof, checked the quartic-versus-quadratic estimates preliminarily, reproduced all exact finite output, and verified six pinned source files, three literature downloads and 29 author artifacts. A fixed-mass motion of the middle target atom also disproves a uniform linear potential estimate, even after optimizing additive constants. These are obstructions to sufficient estimates; they do not refute the desired density-robust cube-root estimate for optimal maps.

A second actual optimal-map example disproves an unscaled source-displacement shortcut for optimal-target gluings. The entropic route proves a uniform conditional-variance estimate and a genuine mass-uniform two-atom bias bound. A feasible non-Gibbs plan shows why small conditional variance alone does not control map bias.

New cluster constructions prove exact invariance under unequal coincident splitting, a mass-weighted symmetric-KL identity, and comparison bounds without label entropy. A source-slice quantile construction yields |sqrt(B)-sqrt(F)| <= sqrt(V), with V <= 2 C L P_K epsilon. Here F measures differences between the Gibbs and hard scalar target laws conditional on each source fiber. The intermediate vector need not be a convex gradient or have the original target law. The proposed bound F <= A epsilon is **unproved** and equivalent to the desired uniform bias bound up to explicit variance constants.

### I38 accepted as R012; sixth substantial finding

The acceptance record preserves the full theorem, source dependencies, proof outline, constants, review decisions and novelty limits. The result is not described as the first quantitative propeller theorem or a sharp-constant theorem. [I39 quantum/spectral discovery](iteration39-quantum-spectral-discovery-task.json) now screens fresh area-law, Haldane and spin-glass/spectral consequences, requiring a substantive new mechanism rather than routine gap or compactness transfers. The ten-finding objective remains active: **six accepted, four remaining**.

The other screens retain distinct scopes. Classical high-temperature SK log-Sobolev control needs an entropy estimate beyond the source's variance transfer; modified LSI is not interchangeable with that target. Critical waiting-time relaxation W asks for uniformity over all sufficiently late finite-size waiting times for both Gaussian and Rademacher disorder, beyond compact-time convergence and relaxation of the limiting process. An exact eight-state reversible chain exhibits a delayed bump despite bounded evolved densities and bounded kernels; it does not satisfy all SK edge hypotheses and does not refute W. Stationary large-lag control is a technical spectral-measure consequence. PEPS existence/accuracy operations use the unknown ground state and an existential column choice, so they do not supply the screened input-to-output algorithm. Bounded-total-strength defects and a boundary-field interval follow technically from Weyl estimates.

The parent read the full report and verifier, checked the Gaussian warming statement and the opening strong-semigroup/weak-density interfaces in the quench source, and reproduced [both commands](../experiments/i39-parent-verification.json). Two mutable ledger changes and the previously recorded removal of one trailing newline from R012 remain explicitly separated from proof dependencies. The diagnostics are exact finite checks, not independent analytic acceptance of the new partial deductions.

I40 independently checks I39's eight-state delayed-bump example. Keeping only its visible coordinate leaves a nonvanishing hidden observable norm; keeping all coordinates makes the limiting dynamics nonergodic. Thus it does not contradict G or model the full SK interfaces. The Rademacher attempts isolate two unpaid estimates: a tight fair-start L2 density at a fixed positive scaled time, and convergence of a positive profile expressible through four times on one stationary trajectory. Together they suffice for W, but neither their necessity nor their completion is claimed. The raw density formula has an exponential endpoint weight outside the source's polynomial test class. Conditional Haar identities are Gaussian-specific; an entropy bound alone also fails to control these growing observables, as shown by a precise two-atom example.

For fair-start warming, I41 derives the positive identity D_J(s)=z_+ E_nu exp(-H(X_(2sT_n))) for the evolved density’s squared L2 norm. Its two-path collision representation has a midpoint tilted by the squared evolved density, and its normalized path law changes both the initial marginal and future intensities. The conjugated Feynman–Kac potential changes sign. Thus neither static replica comparison nor dropping the path weight proves a fixed-positive-time tight bound. The exponential initial annealed moment does not disprove positive-time quenched warming. The fair-start density estimate remains unpaid; it is a sufficient condition for W, not a necessary reformulation.

A technical concavity/first-variation argument identifies equality with identical normalized cone-volume measures and shows that all intermediate measures agree. For polytope equality pairs it fixes the true facet normals and their positive cone-volume weights, but does not fix the whole normal fan. An elementary nonresonance argument classifies equality paths in an open simple chamber when all volume-monomial exponents are distinct. The relevant general block equalities lie on resonant sets, so that restriction does not solve the target.

The other screens preserve their scopes. Fixed-volume cubic-torus quadratic stability follows technically from strict local stability and compactness, even at either phase transition when both minimizer types are included. A uniform estimate measuring only distance to the winning branch fails near a transition. The profile for arbitrary rectangular aspect ratios still requires a new anisotropic endpoint argument. Simplex products do not beat the simplex in dimensions four through eight in the exact finite screen; this excludes only that construction, not general reverse-projection counterexamples. Existing higher-dimensional counterexamples are credited.

The [completed I48 significance review](../reviews/i48-planar-logarithmic-stability-novelty.md) gives **TECHNICAL ONLY**, not EXACT DUPLICATE. The parent retains I47’s independent original-proof PASS. The reduction uses the classical planar inverse sine operator and Bauer–Jost’s weighted dual Cheeger theorem. Crucially, the operator’s ordinary spectral gap controls the mass omitted by the optimizing bipartition; generic near-bipartiteness alone would not. The resulting two groups have uniformly positive total mass, despite arbitrarily small individual facets. Averaging within each group chooses actual active normal directions. Angular mass transport and the linear support formula approximate an enclosing parallelogram at error O(sqrt(D/v)), where D is logarithmic curvature and v is centered slope variance.

The author uses the pinned entropy remainder to bound the nonlinear Gaussian field and normalize its linear coefficients. Distributional curl testing by mollification gives quantitative first jets of the nonlinear matrix field. The inherited Taylor identities then yield approximate coefficient symmetry and commutation. The principal proposed algebraic contribution, Lemma A, converts a symmetric cubic tensor’s small associativity and quadratic-normalization residuals into a linear distance bound to a normalized orthogonal decomposition. A global cubic maximizer creates a spectral separation, while successive restrictions add only quadratic residual errors. A second spectral-partition construction gives a weaker explicit power. Gaussian Poincaré reconstructs the law; the source’s affine lower bound and a covariance comparison remove the normalization, and weighted approximation handles arbitrary densities.

The audit expands the distributional-curl interpolation and Gaussian-to-Lebesgue conversion, exact jet signs and coefficient symmetrization, the global cubic maximum and quadratic restriction errors, simultaneous rotation of tensor indices, the deflation bootstrap and final squared-error budget. It checks the separate spectral induction, covariance cross-moment orientation, uniform affine inverse bound and nonsmooth weighted approximation. These are verifications of the written mechanism rather than replacement proofs needed to repair it.

The [completed I29 report](i29-common-base-entropy.md), returned after the later discovery rounds, proves at author level the rank-sharp inequality H_C(x) ≥ F(x)−(1−1/r)B(x) for every feasible mean x of the common bases of two labelled rank-r matroids, r≥1. Here H_C is the maximum entropy of a realizing law, F=−Σx_i log x_i, and B=−Σ(1−x_i)log(1−x_i). Rank zero is treated separately. The Gibbs and weighted partition-function consequences retain that maximum-entropy qualifier; the statement is false for arbitrary laws with the same mean.

The review checks simultaneous rotation of all three coefficient indices at the paired Gaussian points, including repeated eigenvalues and the evaluated-field derivative sign. The fourth-moment crossing term can be negative; its row-column norm bound is the valid argument. The three-slot tails act on fixed tensors before expansion, so no unproved input-slot energy cap or independence between slots is used. The repair is tested where symmetrization actually creates an eigenvalue above the cutoff. The covariance normalization argument avoids squaring an order inequality between two unrelated positive matrices. The exact source weight remains quadratically coercive on each fixed bounded spectral interval.
### I64 integration and R014 acceptance: uniform coefficient compatibility

The [completed independent contribution review](../reviews/i64-entropy-coefficient-extraction-novelty.md) gives **SUBSTANTIAL** for CE61's uniform implication from averaged nonlinear curl to total coefficient symmetry and commutator residual. The parent accepts [R014](../findings/R014-uniform-coefficient-extraction.md) as the **eighth substantial finding**, with the symmetric bounded-energy repair and capped entropy reduction included once. The fixed energy cap is retained; neither AR nor U is accepted.

The comparison credits the actual entropy, Mahler, Gamma and Kadison–Kastler proof operations, including divided differences, tensor rotation, positive spectral measures and fourth-moment clipping. Bathory's nonlinear derivative pairing is a particularly close antecedent: it compares inner products of whole transformed matrices, whereas CE61's curl first subtracts differently weighted tensor entries. The parent read that paired-conjugation proof and the explicit full-gradient commutator surplus. The missing projected-cancellation comparison is supplied by CE61's two equations, with tails controlled uniformly for all three slots. Its ingredients are elementary; the substantive conclusion is the growing-dimensional compatibility implication on the exact analytic quantity available from the sharp entropy source. No claim of a new functional calculus or worldwide priority follows.
